timeline: You are looking at Gujarat's Modhera Sun Temple, engineered around 1026 CE to direct equinox sunbeams into its sanctum.
King Bhima the First commissioned this stone complex.
Craftsmen sculpted intricate stone carvings throughout the complex.
Fifty-two carved pillars frame the assembly hall.
During equinoxes, dawn rays hit the doorway.
The beam pierces straight into the garbhagriha.
At summer solstice noon, it casts zero shadow.
Yet an upside-down stone inscription marks destruction.
Active worship ended here centuries ago.
Today, silent steps surround the quiet reservoir.
And each spring, sunrise repeats its ancient alignment.
